BiblicalUsage: Ephes-Dammim — the edge of blood — is the place where the Philistines camped when they gathered to fight Israel, between Socoh and Azekah. It is the ground where David and Goliath would meet, and the name fits the blood that would be shed there.
TheologicalSignificance: Where armies gather, blood follows, and it was on that edge that a shepherd boy trusted God instead of armour. I believe the place name is no accident: the edge of blood became the field where faith beat the sword.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
